brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Spatial cluster metaphor with dashed category zones reads instantly and supports the brief of proximity-based organization over lists
Consistent card vocabulary — emoji-glyph tile, title, timestamp, snippet, tag — gives a clean repeatable atom across the canvas
Minimap in lower-right is a thoughtful navigational affordance that signals the canvas is meant to scale beyond viewport
dominant_weaknesses: Cards overlap and clip text ('GraphQL schema and...', 'Legacy Componen...') making the layout feel accidental rather than spatially intentional
Emoji icons on colored squares clash tonally with the otherwise restrained slate typography, fragmenting the visual system
Category labels, tags, and timestamps share too-similar gray weights, flattening hierarchy and making zones blur into each other
fix_priorities: Resolve card overlaps and truncation with a real spatial grid or force-directed layout that guarantees breathing room
Replace emoji glyphs with a unified monoline icon set or typographic markers to restore systemic coherence
Strengthen hierarchy: bolder zone titles, lighter tags, and clearer connector lines between related documents
Introduce subtle zone tinting or topology so proximity reads as semantic, not just decorative grouping
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept (spatial knowledge map) outpaces visceral polish and behavioral clarity, where overlap and truncation undermine trust.
rationale.intent_fit: It gestures at the spatial-canvas brief through clustered zones and a minimap, but cards behave like loose grids inside boxes rather than truly proximity-driven artifacts.
